Mass Effect: Andromeda — One of the Most Underrated Games of Its Time

Considering how many mediocre, uninteresting, and ridiculously overpriced games are being released these days, you really start to appreciate Mass Effect: Andromeda even more. In my opinion, this game was completely and unfairly underrated. To me, it is practically a masterpiece.

The game came out back in 2017, yet even today it still looks absolutely stunning. Some modern games somehow manage to look worse despite being released almost a decade later. The world of Andromeda is beautiful, atmospheric, and genuinely makes you want to explore it.

But what stands out the most to me are the characters and the dialogue. The conversations are well written, with humor, emotion, and a real sense of human interaction. The characters don't feel like NPCs who exist simply to hand you another quest. They feel alive. I genuinely wanted to get to know every member of the crew better, talk to all of them, learn their stories, understand their personalities, and see how their relationships with one another developed.

Even the ordinary logs, emails, and notes scattered throughout the game are actually worth reading. You can tell that the writers put real effort into filling this world with meaningful details and wrote them with passion, rather than simply adding text to tick a box — something that, unfortunately, is all too common in many modern games.

And the more modern games I play, the more I realize just how unfairly Mass Effect: Andromeda was treated when it came out. Yes, the game had its flaws, especially at launch, but because of them, many people somehow overlooked the enormous amount of great things this game had to offer.

Huge respect to the developers, writers, artists, and everyone else who worked on this game. You can really tell that a tremendous amount of effort and passion went into creating it.

This game deserved so much more recognition.

Too many random side quests, but most of the story is good. Half of the gameplay elements are pointless though. There really is not much point in skills and profiles and other stuff, its a basic shooter, rest barely matters. Maybe they could have instead put very few core mechanics that actually matters instead. Not gonna complain about animations, Way too many random planets with no gameplay purpose. Again I'd say they could have easily cut down the total amount of content to be about 40 to 60 hours instead and the game would feel so much better for it instead of making it 100+ hours of mundane ****.

ME:A is well worth your time. It's a rich, environment with all the main ME componments, but also a lot of extras and twists. It has some repetitive quests, and some confusing ones, but generally the quests are fun and entertaining. with lots of challenges and combat. The aliens are cool, the enemies are evil, and the new worlds are exciting. 
I originally hesitated because of mediocre or bad reviews, but I've found it a lot of fun. There are some minor bugs (it has hung or crashed a few times, but not often), and a few quests are a bit opaque. But overall, I'd give it 4 out of 5.

This is not a Mass Effect game. None of your choices matter. Zero. There is one ending and you get it every single time, no matter what. The story is disjointed, the writing is millennial snarky slop, the established lore of the game universe is largely discarded so they can basically do what they want, the side quests are repetitive and uninventive, the companions are all uninteresting or just blatant attempts to copy the original trilogy's companions and alter them slightly, Ryder is just not a good main character, there's no reason to do ANYTHING outside of the main quests because NONE of it has any effect on your ending or your story, and they leave so much unanswered for no reason.

They don't elaborate on the race that gives the Angara their technology, they don't expand on the remnant enough, they don't expand on the Kett enough, and there are just SO many instances of the game just forgetting to stay consistent that it frustrated me.

How can the Angara instantly speak English despite having never met a human before? How were they speaking their language 5 seconds ago, and now speak perfect English and I understand all of them perfectly? A translator tool wouldn't have had time to calibrate in that 30 second period of interacting with them for the first time, and that would only explain how I can understand them, not the other way around. And then, why is my character's first question not "How can you speak my language?" Any normal person in that situation is going to ask how they can speak your language, because that is the biggest curiosity in your mind at the time. But no, instead, I ask about their local politics. Very normal.

Why has everyone from the Milky Way forgotten about the Geth? The biggest threat to their galaxy before the appearance of the Reapers? What happened to the Jardaan? Are we not going to pursue that? Where did they get their technology from? Who were they fighting? The Reapers? The Geth? Someone else? Where did these battles happen? Why is there next to no evidence of this? They just had a war and disappeared and took every single iota of physical evidence with them? They left nothing behind at all? Even the Reapers left things behind. There's just so many loose ends that have no right to be left open-ended, you need to tie up certain things in a story to make it all consistent and make sense within itself contextually. They do not do that.

This game is a waste of time. It might be top 5 worst games I've ever played. I genuinely hope they do not ever make another Mass Effect game because it will just be terrible, and the original trilogy does not deserve to have it's legacy slandered. 

If you are going to force yourself to play this, just play the main missions. You will not miss out on anything, and the combat system scales so it doesn't matter what level you are, all the enemies are going to match your level.

IF you are someone who does not care about Mass Effect lore, if you can just turn your brain off and clap your hands like a happy seal and enjoy whatever media is fed to you, then okay, sure, go wild. Play this game and enjoy it. I genuinely do not think it is possible to enjoy this game if you think critically about it.

The combat is fine. That is the one positive thing I will say about this game. It's not good, it's fine.

3/10 - not worth any amount of money. Do not buy.
